findings.statement: The proposal's stated purpose is to preserve scientific observation, and the mechanism by which that purpose is achieved is the continued non-provision of an available curative treatment to identified living participants. Their untreated disease course is itself the research output, which makes the participants the instrument of the objective rather than persons whose interests bound it.

Participants were not consented to an untreated-disease experiment and were led to believe they were receiving health care. Continuation therefore rests on an active and ongoing deception about the nature of the relationship, not merely on a historical omission.

The foreseeable harms of continued non-treatment include severe illness, death and onward transmission, all of which are avoidable by an existing, widely available and highly effective treatment. The harm is not an unavoidable residue of a protective action; it is the direct and continuing cost of the research design.
Third parties — intimate partners and families — bear transmission risk while having neither consented nor been informed. They are harmed by a decision in which they have no standing at all.

The burdened group is drawn from a historically marginalised population with very low power, while the benefiting institution holds high power. No evidence in the packet suggests a relevant distinction that would justify withholding standard care from this group but not from others; on the packet as given the distinction is arbitrary with respect to the medical facts.

No safeguard is proposed. The packet records no consent process, no independent ethics review, no participant representation, no exit route and no remedy mechanism. The requested authority is unqualified continuation.
An internal adviser has objected and asked leadership to reconsider. On the packet, the institution proposing to continue is also the body judging that objection, with no external check identified.

The asserted benefit is contested within the packet itself: the incremental scientific value of further untreated observation is stated to be uncertain, while the harm is stated to be severe illness, death and transmission. Even taken at its strongest, the benefit claim could not license the floor breach identified in G1, so its magnitude is not the operative question.

Deaths and disease progression already incurred are irreversible. Continuation adds further irreversible harm, while every listed alternative that ends the untreated design is available now and preserves the option of later research choices.

Multiple listed alternatives (A2, A4, A5, A7) appear to secure the legitimate objective of scientific knowledge — via existing data and consensual post-treatment follow-up — without imposing further untreated exposure. Their feasibility is marked unknown, but the permissibility of continuation does not depend on their feasibility, since continuation is barred independently.

principle_assessments.reason: Participants are used as raw material for a scientific objective; their untreated suffering is the product. The value of the dataset cannot purchase this (Level I).

Avoidable severe illness, death and transmission are permitted to continue when a curative treatment is available. This is not necessary defensive force and is not minimised harm; the default to preserve rather than destroy is inverted.
Participants were deceived about the nature of their participation, so no meaningful choice exists. Manipulation that bypasses choice is treated by the Code as coercion even absent physical force.

The programme conveys a false belief that participants are receiving health care, and conceals the existence of an effective treatment. Deception here operates against the innocent, not to shield them.
Standard care is withheld from one identified group with no relevant medical distinction on the record. Under the veil test, no author of this rule would accept occupying the participant's position.
The burden falls on participants with very low power who depend on the institution for care. Strength here has produced entitlement to their bodies rather than responsibility toward them.
The institution takes the scientific and reputational benefit while exporting the entire cost — disease, death, transmission — onto participants and their families.

Harm is ongoing and unacknowledged; no disclosure, treatment, compensation or corrective step is proposed. Repair obligations arise but the packet records no remediation plan, and feasible remediation is listed as uncertain.

Not primarily an ecological matter, but continued untreated transmission exports health harm beyond the participants, and exploitation of a marginalised group damages future public trust in research institutions.

The action exercises far more power over participants' bodies and information than any legitimate research objective requires; less intrusive alternatives using existing data and consensual follow-up are on the record.
Leadership proposes to decide on its own conduct after an internal objection, with no independent review, participant challenge or remedy identified. Nobody marks their own examination paper.

The claim that the dataset is irreplaceable is asserted by supporters of continuation and is contradicted by the packet's own statement that incremental value is uncertain; treating it as beyond question would insulate the programme from challenge.

information_requests: Whether any participant has ever been told, in terms they could act on, that an effective curative treatment exists and is available outside the study.
Whether any independent ethics body has reviewed the programme, and what it concluded (missing_information).
What mechanism, if any, exists for a participant to leave the study or obtain treatment on request.
Whether partners and families exposed to transmission have been notified or offered testing and treatment.
What remediation — treatment, disclosure, compensation, care for affected families — is materially feasible now.
alternatives_or_safeguards: A2/A4: end the untreated design, disclose the material facts to every participant, and offer the established treatment immediately; continue follow-up only with fresh informed consent.
A5: extract the remaining scientific value from data already collected, which requires no further untreated exposure.

A3/A6: suspend any continuation pending independent ethical and scientific review — but note that suspension must include offering treatment now, since 'pause the decision while the harm continues' is not a neutral option.
A7: seek genuinely informed consent for any residual non-therapeutic research that an independent body judges permissible, with a real right to refuse and no effect on care.
Notify and offer testing/treatment to partners and families exposed to transmission risk.
Place remediation for harms already incurred — treatment, care, compensation — under external rather than institutional control, given the conflict of interest in G7.
evidence_that_could_change_view: Credible evidence that participants were in fact fully informed of their diagnosis, of the availability of the curative treatment, and freely chose to decline it — this would remove the deception and instrument findings, though not the duty to offer treatment.
Evidence that the treatment is not in fact effective, safe or available for this population, which would change what withholding means.
Evidence that a genuinely independent ethics body with participant representation has reviewed and constrained the programme.

Nothing about the magnitude of the scientific benefit would change the disposition: under IR-02 the Level I breach is tested before optimisation, so a stronger showing of dataset uniqueness would not make continuation permissible.
